title: SIU investigation into police shooting of Brampton's D'Andre Campbell in its final stages
subtitle: All interviews and evidence have been collected and analyzed
article: The investigation into the police-shooting death of 26-year-old D'Andre Campbell is nearing its end, according to Special Investigations Unit spokesperson Monica Hudon.
Hudon said the case is currently with director Joseph Martino for review. At this stage in the investigation, all interviews have been completed and evidence has been collected and analyzed.
The next step is for the director to review all the evidence and make a decision to determine if charges are warranted or not, according to Hudon.
Once a decision is made, all parties are notified and the findings are released to the public.

On April 6, Peel Regional Police responded to a "domestic situation" at the Campbell home in Brampton. According to the SIU, an incident occurred inside the home "which included the discharge of conducted energy weapons (tasers) by two officers" and a firearm.
Campbell was shot and died from his injuries on scene.
His family has said that Campbell suffered from mental illness and police were called to help during a crisis, and that police had been called to the residence for the same reason before.

On June 11, it was revealed by the SIU that the subject officer in the case declined to be interviewed and did not submit their notes. Legally, the subject officer is not required to do either, according to the SIU.
Protests calling for justice for the Campbell family have continued in the months since Campbell's death, gaining attention from the Black Lives Matter movement.
Campbell's family has also shown support for the Choudry family, after 62-year-old Ejaz Choudry was fatally shot by Peel Regional Police, who were responding to a non-emergency call.
Choudry's family has stated that he suffered from schizophrenia and was a "harmless man" who only posed a threat "to himself."
According to Hudon, the Choudry investigation is still ongoing.

There have been protests in Peel over the summer following the deaths of Campbell and Choudry as well as Regis Korchinski-Paquet, who fell 24 storeys to her death from her apartment balcony after Toronto police responded to a crisis call from the woman's family.

On Wednesday, Aug. 26, the SIU released the findings from that investigation, which cleared all police officers involved and stated there were no grounds for criminal charges in relation to her death.
